title: Etale charts of decent spaces lift generalizations
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Assume that every point of $|X|$ is represented by a quasi-compact monomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$ for some field $F$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Monomorphism means that composition is injective on morphisms from every algebraic space over $S$; quasi-compact means that after every scheme test inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. Let $p:U\to X$ be a representable etale morphism from a scheme, with etaleness tested after scheme base change [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Write $z\leadsto z_0$ when $z_0$ belongs to the closure of $\{z\}$. For every $u_0\in U$ and $x\in|X|$ with $x\leadsto p(u_0)$, there exists $u\in U$ such that $u\leadsto u_0$ and $p(u)=x$. No quasi-separatedness, surjectivity, finite-type or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03IL (lemma-decent-specialization); decency is expressed here by the quasi-compact field-monomorphism condition.

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $W\subset U$ of $u_0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. Write $a:W\to X$ for the restriction of $p$. It is representable etale: on every scheme test it is an open immersion followed by the tested etale map, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation](1),(2) applies. The image $I=a(W)$ is open and $a:W\to I$ is continuous and open by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Since $a(u_0)\in I$ and $x\leadsto a(u_0)$, the definition of closure implies $x\in I$. Put $R=W\times_XW$ with projections $s,t$. The sheaf fibre-product construction [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] and the scheme-test definition [def-trf-algebraic-space] make $R$ a scheme and $s,t$ etale. In particular they are flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tag 03K2, lemma-specialization, first paragraph; Tag 03IL reduces to this argument.

proof.text: Take the quasi-compact field monomorphism $j:T=\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$ representing $x$ supplied by the hypothesis. Set $P=W\times_XT$. The scheme-test definition [def-trf-algebraic-space] makes $P\to T$ etale. Quasi-compactness of $j$ makes $P\to W$ quasi-compact. Since $W$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], taking the inverse image of the whole open $W$ shows that $P$ is quasi-compact. The unique point of $T$ has residue field $F$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so the fibre of $P\to T$ there is $P$ itself by the identity-base-change universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] makes $|P|$ discrete. Its cover by open singletons has a finite subcover, so $|P|$ is finite. The image formula of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] identifies the image of $|P|\to W$ with $A=a^{-1}(\{x\})$. Hence $A$ is finite; it is nonempty because $x\in I$.

source.place: Tag 03JV, lemma-UR-finite-above-x, (4) implies (5) implies (1), restricted to the chart fibre; Tag 03K2, finite fibre at the general point.

proof.text: Let $C=\bigcup_{w\in A}\overline{\{w\}}\subset W$. This is closed because $A$ is finite. We claim $s^{-1}(C)=t^{-1}(C)$. If $s(r)\in C$, choose $w\in A$ with $w\leadsto s(r)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] to the flat scheme morphism $s$ to obtain $r'\leadsto r$ with $s(r')=w$. The equation $a s=a t$ gives $a(t(r'))=x$, hence $t(r')\in A$. Continuity of $t$, supplied by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus], gives $t(r')\leadsto t(r)$, so $t(r)\in C$. Interchanging $s,t$ proves the reverse implication. This proves the claim without needing any finiteness assumption on the relation fibre.

source.place: Tag 03K2, lemma-specialization: the flat-lifting argument showing invariance of the finite-fibre closure; the same argument directly gives equality of inverse images.

proof.text: The point-surjectivity assertion of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] says that whenever $v,w\in W$ have $a(v)=a(w)$, some $r\in R$ has $s(r)=v$ and $t(r)=w$. The equality from step 3 therefore says $C$ is saturated: $v\in C$ if and only if $w\in C$. Consequently $I\setminus a(C)=a(W\setminus C)$. Indeed, a point outside $a(C)$ has every lift outside $C$, and a point with a lift outside $C$ has no lift inside $C$ by saturation. The right side is open by the openness assertion of the same node. Thus $a(C)$ is closed in $I$.

source.place: Tag 03K2, lemma-specialization: the invariant closed set descends to a closed subset of the open chart image; spaces-properties.tex Tags 03H4 and 03BX.

proof.text: Every point of $A$ belongs to $C$, so $x\in a(C)$. The relation $x\leadsto a(u_0)$ remains a specialization in the open subspace $I$, because both points lie in $I$ and closure in a subspace is intersection with the ambient closure. Since $a(C)$ is closed in $I$, it contains $a(u_0)$. Choose $v\in C$ above $a(u_0)$; saturation gives $u_0\in C$. The defining finite union for $C$ therefore supplies $u\in A$ with $u\leadsto u_0$ in $W$. The open inclusion $W\subset U$ is continuous, so this specialization also holds in $U$, and $p(u)=a(u)=x$.

source.place: Tag 03K2, lemma-specialization, end of first proof paragraph, with saturation selecting the prescribed endpoint directly; this proves Tag 03IL.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03IL (lemma-decent-specialization), 03JV (lemma-UR-finite-above-x), and 03K2 (lemma-specialization). The invariant-closure argument uses only finiteness of the chart fibre.

Generic point-fibre-product surjectivity, continuity and openness descend a saturated closed subset; no six-functor theorem replaces this foundation. This is a generic tool, and the unit has no replacement for it.
Generic sheaf fibre products construct the chart relation, with no use of a trace-formula argument. This is a generic tool, and the unit has no replacement for it.
An affine chart is quasi-compact, needed to test the given quasi-compact field map. This is a generic tool, and the unit has no replacement for it.

lean.statement: theorem exists_generalization_of_decent_of_isEtale {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hdecent : ∀ x : Point X.obj.obj, ∃ (K : Type u) (_ : Field K) (b : Spec (CommRingCat.of K) ⟶ S) (i : yoneda.obj (Over.mk b) ⟶ X.obj.obj), schemePointMap i (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x ∧ (∀ (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (f g : Y.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk b)), f ≫ i = g ≫ i → f = g) ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ q ↦ QuasiCompact q.left) i) (U : Over S) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (hp : IsEtale p) (u₀ : U.left) (x : Point X.obj.obj) (hx : schemePointMap p u₀ ∈ closure ({x} : Set (Point X.obj.obj))) : ∃ u : U.left, u₀ ∈ closure ({u} : Set U.left) ∧ schemePointMap p u = x
